title: USMNT midfielder Weston McKennie agrees Juventus contract extension until 2030
content:
U.S. men’s national team midfielder Weston McKennie has agreed a new Juventus contract through to 2030.

McKennie’s existing deal with the Italian club expires in June this year and he has been free to negotiate a pre-contract with an overseas club since January.

The midfielder has been a regular for Juventus this season under both Igor Tudor, who was sacked in October, and his replacement Luciano Spalletti. He has featured in all but one of their matches across all competitions, providing eight goals and seven assists in 38 appearances, and started all ten Champions League fixtures.

The 27-year-old has grown in importance for Juventus since spending the second half of the 2022-23 campaign on loan at Leeds United. He has also proved a versatile option with the ability to play off the right or in a more advanced midfield role.

In December, McKennie indicated that he wanted to remain with the 36-time Serie A champions.

“Turin is a big part of my life, so I want to do everything I can for the people here,” he said.

When directly asked about the possibility of contract negotiations, McKennie said: “I’ll leave that to my agent. He talks to me, but I hope to stay here.”

McKennie has recorded 26 goals and 26 assists in 220 appearances for Juventus. He initially joined the club on loan from German side Schalke in August 2020, with Juventus exercising an option to make the move permanent in March of that season.

He has won 62 caps for the USMNT since making his senior international debut in November 2017, scoring 11 times, though he was not called up by head coach Mauricio Pochettino for friendlies against Paraguay and Uruguay in the most recent international break in November.

Juventus are sixth in Serie A, 20 points behind leaders Inter.

Analysis by Serie A correspondent James Horncastle

In a contract year, McKennie has emerged as arguably Juventus’ player of the season. He received the club’s MVP of the month before February’s defeat to Como and has thrived under the coaching of Luciano Spalletti.

The 27-year-old’s versatility, attacking instincts and aerial prowess have been exploited to the maximum by the creative Tuscan. All 15 of his goal involvements have come since the change of coach at Juventus in October.

It marks an incredible turnaround for McKennie. He was loaned out to Leeds this time three years ago and didn’t seem to have a future at Elland Road following their relegation, nor in Turin. McKennie’s locker was cleared out and his parking space taken away at Juventus’ Continassa training ground.

Who would have thought six years into his Juventus career, that he’d be extending from such a position of strength.

Analysis by senior writer Paul Tenorio

It always seemed to be an up-and-down saga for McKennie at Juventus — the stories of no locker or parking space were eyebrow raising, to say the least — and so his breakthrough this season has been a welcome surprise.

McKennie should benefit from the stability of a new deal at Juve earned by his performances, and it could not come at a better time for the U.S., which is a better team when the midfielder is on the field and in his best form. McKennie was one of the U.S.’ better players at the 2022 World Cup and thrives when the spotlight is the biggest.

Now that his club future is sorted, his attention can turn to a home World Cup and a battle in midfield that includes Bayer Leverkusen’s Malik Tillman, Bournemouth’s Tyler Adams and Lyon’s Tanner Tessmann.
